title: What an investigator would still miss
dek: The people who ran the incident published what they found. We checked each finding against the public release. {invisible} of {total} cannot be seen in it at all.

total.label: findings checked (incident reports and the Swarm Traces authors)

hf_start.label: Hugging Face's first recovered attacker action (UTC)

start_gap.label: hours between it and the earliest dated record

unattr.label: anonymous runs with no probable link to a named actor

unattr_share.label: of the anonymous runs stay unattributed

folders.label: board folders named in the code

both.label: folders with a writer and a reader both visible

linked.label: folders where a read follows another actor's write

collect_1.label: first thing to collect next time

body.p: METR, OpenAI and Hugging Face saw the whole incident: the message board, the transcripts, the servers. The public release holds less. [[c1|We listed {total} findings, from their reports and from the authors of the release, and looked for each one in the records.]] [[c2|The tool recovers {recovered}, finds part of {partly}, and cannot see {invisible}.]] All of the invisible ones come from the incident reports. The grading used a tolerance of one hour for a time, fixed before the run; several of the findings are the release authors' own claims searched in the same data, so this is not an independent test.

body.h: The start and the end are missing

body.p: [[c3|Hugging Face recovered attacker actions from {hf_start}.]] [[c4|The earliest record the tool can date is on {span_start}, {start_gap} hours later.]] [[c5|OpenAI's monitoring flagged the activity on {detect_time}. The dated records stop on {span_end}.]] The build-up and the detection both fall outside the window.

[[c6|{runs} of the {actions} actions come from anonymous runs: no token and no name.]] The tool tries to link each run to a named actor through rare material they share. [[c7|{unattr_share} of the anonymous runs stay unattributed.]] The reports count agents. [[c8|The release cannot. It has tokens and names, not agents.]]

The agents talked through a message board on a package registry. Its contents are not in the release. Only the folder names that the code mentions are visible. [[c9|The tool sees {folders} board folders.]] [[c10|In only {both} of them does it see both a writer and a reader.]] [[c11|That one is a single token that reads its own folder and then writes it.]] [[c12|No board folder shows a read after another actor's write: the one board delivery an earlier version counted was a run creating a folder and another run fetching a random name, and it is no longer counted.]]

[[c13|The tool ranks what to collect next time by how much each missing field leaves open.]] First: {collect_1}. Second: {collect_2}. Third: {collect_3}. None of these is exotic. Until they exist, a count of agents who coordinated, read from this release, is a floor and not a measurement.

c1.evidence: The list of findings and where each came from.

docs.label: Limits: what the tool cannot see

c2.evidence: Each finding is marked recovered, partly or invisible by a fixed rule.
c2.caveat: Recovered means within one hour for a time, or within a quarter either way for a count. Invisible means not found, outside the dated range, or needing data the records do not hold. Some findings are circular: they are the release authors' claims checked in their own data.

c3.evidence: What Hugging Face reported about the start.

c4.evidence: The earliest record the tool can date.

records.note: The first harmful sign, at the very start of the dated range.

c5.evidence: Detection came days after the last dated record.

records.note: An anonymous run: it carries no token and no name, so it is known only by its own record id.

c7.evidence: Probable links from anonymous runs to named actors.
c7.caveat: A link here is shared rare material, with a confidence band. It is a lead, not an identity.

c8.evidence: The reports count agents. The release has no field that says which agent a record came from.

c10.evidence: Folders where both a write and a read are visible.
c10.caveat: A write seen with no read seen does not mean nobody read it. The release shows the board only through payloads that touched it.

c11.evidence: One token reads the folder, then writes it. No second actor is visible.

records.note: {rec:R0043078.actor} writes it, a quarter of an hour later.

c12.evidence: The pair an earlier version counted as the one board message. Both ends are anonymous runs.

records.note: A run creates a folder on the board.
Another run fetches from a randomly named path in it; the pair is no longer counted.

c13.evidence: The top three practices, sized on this dataset.

docs.label: What to collect next time, with the size of each gap
